protocol: A: q_j=sigma/sigma_y=beta/r; unclipped unrestricted OLS affine ddof=0 identity; do not mix with clip[0,100] LS-affine. B: p=clip(yhat/100,1e-5,1-1e-5); one global phi BB vs Binomial vs max-r/min-MAE; hits/n_words likelihood labels only. D: z-score max-r then LS = reparameterization/control, not a new algorithm. Sanity1 mean-only vs std-only; Sanity2 1% lattice + continuous vs 5% grid.

identity_dev.proposition: Same DEV, unclipped unrestricted OLS affine, ddof=0 population moments: min_{a,b} (1/n) Σ(y-aŷ-b)^2 = σ_y^2 (1-r^2). Therefore min affine-MSE ≡ max |r|. This equals max Pearson r only if every candidate has r>0. Do not mix with clip[0,100] LS-affine.

binomial.note: max Binomial likelihood on DEV; one global p_i from ŷ_w/100

D.label: reparameterization/control — NOT a new algorithm
D.explanation: On the continuous nonnegative cone, max-r(Σ α_j x_j) is a ray-equivalent of max-r(Σ β_j z_j) via β_j = α_j σ_j. Simplex (sum-to-1) plus 5% grid can differ; do not package z-score + LS as a method.

sanity1.prediction: std-only explains the large majority of |Δβ| disappearance

sanity2.purpose: exclude 'the alignment result is only because the grid changed'
